---
title: "Tracking Error and Attribution — Did the Portfolio Beat Its Benchmark?"
description: "Explain portfolio mathematics with a small numerical example and practical risk limitations."
---

## The question

**Your bond portfolio gained 3% while its benchmark gained 2%. Does that mean the manager is consistently skilful?**

One good period is not enough. **Active return** compares portfolio and benchmark on the same interval; **tracking error** describes how variable those active returns are; attribution tries to explain their sources.

## Build one relationship

$$
a_t=R_{p,t}-R_{b,t}
$$

**Explain every symbol:** a_t is active return in period t; R_p,t is portfolio return and R_b,t benchmark return over exactly the same period. Positive means outperformance for that period.

**Substitute concrete numbers:** Period 1: portfolio +3%, benchmark +2%, so active return +1 percentage point. Period 2: portfolio +1%, benchmark +2%, so active return −1 percentage point. Their mean is zero, even though the first period looked strong.

## Why this matters for decisions

For these two periods, using the *population* standard deviation convention, tracking error is sqrt(((+0.01−0)²+(−0.01−0)²)/2)=**1% per observation period**. The observed mean active return was 0: there is risk without persistent excess performance in this toy sample.

~~~python
from finance_lab import tracking_error
print(tracking_error([.01,-.01])) # .01
~~~

These minimal examples build on the [Finance calculation lab](../examples/index.qmd), where relevant.

## What the model leaves out

Standard deviation requires a sample-versus-population convention and, when annualised, a sampling-frequency and serial-correlation assumption. Real fixed-income attribution may separate curve carry, curve moves, key-rate shocks, credit spreads, FX, allocation and security selection, with residual effects depending on model.

**Source basis:** Luenberger Investment Science 2e Chs. 9–10 (data/statistics and risk); Fabozzi Handbook 8e Ch. 3 (bond benchmarks) and Part 10 (return attribution).. Text and examples are independently developed.
